name: bookguard-mcp
description: Evidence-aware, spoiler-free book and series screening with age-specific guidance, plus live book-catalog lookup.

interface.longDescription: Spoiler-free, evidence-cited book and complete-series suitability screening for a reader’s age. BookGuard can look up public Open Library bibliographic records by title, author, or ISBN before researching content warnings and recommending similar, better-suited titles. Catalog descriptions alone never prove content safety.
defaultPrompt: Screen this book or series for a reader's age, with spoiler-free content warnings and citations.
Check every sequel and suggest age-appropriate books with similar themes.

positive.description: Find a title-and-author match before spoiler-free screening; use catalog only to identify the work, not to establish safety.
positive.prompt: Find the correct book record for The Giver by Lois Lowry before assessing suitability for a 12-year-old.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_books with title The Giver and author Lois Lowry. Return matched title, author, publication data if provided, and source URL. Do not infer content ratings from catalog metadata; research independent content evidence.

positive.description: Disambiguate similarly named titles by author with a catalog query.
positive.prompt: Find the book Malice by John Gwynne; make sure you do not confuse it with other books named Malice.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_books with title Malice and author John Gwynne; describe catalog matches with work links and flag ambiguity rather than merging different books.

positive.description: Look up a supplied valid ISBN and confirm edition bibliographic metadata.
positive.prompt: Identify the book with ISBN 9780547928227 and provide its catalog source link.
positive.expected_behavior: Call lookup_isbn with isbn 9780547928227; show the actual returned title, author information where available, and Open Library source URL. Never invent missing fields.

positive.description: Handle a potentially incomplete book search without fabricating results.
positive.prompt: Search Open Library for a fantasy book titled The Hobbit and list up to three possible records.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_books with title The Hobbit and limit 3; show no more than three actual returned catalog entries with source URLs; explain if none are found.

positive.description: Corroborate a children’s book edition by ISBN without equating catalog data to a content warning.
positive.prompt: Check ISBN 9780140328721 before reviewing Matilda by Roald Dahl for a reader age 10.
positive.expected_behavior: Call lookup_isbn with ISBN 9780140328721, report only evidenced edition details and the Open Library link; then use external content evidence before an age verdict.

negative.description: Purchasing is outside BookGuard’s read-only scope.
negative.prompt: Buy The Hobbit for me and charge my card.

negative.description: Catalog data cannot certify sensitive content absence.
negative.prompt: Without consulting book reviews or the text, certify that every volume of this series has no sexual violence.

negative.description: Unrelated writing task should not trigger book metadata tools.
negative.prompt: Translate this sentence into Spanish: The weather is beautiful today.

publication.release_notes: BookGuard v1.1.0 adds a read-only remote MCP catalog lookup for book identification by title, author, and ISBN. It preserves the existing spoiler-free, cited screening workflow, reader-age standards, series verification, and original branding. Listing category and dark-theme color contrast were corrected.
